Estimation of Generalized Linear Gaussian Process Models

Source: R/parameter_estimation.R
glgpm.Rd

Fits generalized linear Gaussian process models to spatial data, incorporating spatial Gaussian processes with a Matern correlation function. Supports Gaussian, binomial, Poisson and negative binomial response families.

Usage

glgpm(
  formula,
  data,
  family,
  invlink = NULL,
  denominator = NULL,
  model_crs = NULL,
  distance_units = c("km", "m"),
  control_mcmc = set_control_mcmc(),
  control_mcml = set_control_mcml(),
  seed = NULL,
  return_samples = TRUE,
  messages = getOption("RiskMap.messages", TRUE),
  fix_var_me = NULL,
  start_pars = list(beta = NULL, sigma2 = NULL, tau2 = NULL, phi = NULL, sigma2_me =
    NULL, sigma2_re = NULL)
)

Arguments

formula

A formula object specifying the model to be fitted. The formula should include fixed effects and spatial effects specified using gp() and optionally, random effects specified using re(). It can also include one offset() term that names a column of data, e.g. offset(log_exposure).

data

An sf object containing the variables in the model.

family

The distribution of the response given the random effects, with its link. Either one of the strings "gaussian", "binomial" and "poisson", which take the identity, logit and log links, a family object as in stats::glm(), such as binomial("probit"), or negative_binomial() for overdispersed counts with the log link, whose size is estimated unless a value is given (negative_binomial(theta = 2) or MASS::negative.binomial(2)). Where nothing is estimated, as in specify_glgpm(), the size must be given. Binomial responses take the logit, probit, complementary log-log ("cloglog") and Cauchy ("cauchit") links, Poisson responses the log link and Gaussian responses the identity link. binomial("log") and poisson("identity") are not accepted, because they can give means outside the range of the family, nor is poisson("sqrt"), whose inverse gives the same mean to a positive and a negative linear predictor. Quasi-likelihood families, such as stats::quasibinomial(), have no likelihood to maximise and are not accepted either. Any other link can be given in invlink. A named link gives the same estimates as its inverse given in invlink, and is faster when that inverse cannot be differentiated symbolically, as for invlink = pnorm.

invlink

A function that maps the linear predictor to the mean of the response given the random effects, for a binomial or Poisson model whose link is not one of those that family names, such as a link for an imperfect diagnostic test. Its first and second derivatives are found symbolically where possible and numerically otherwise. They only steer the importance sampler, so they affect the speed of a fit and not its estimates. Not applicable for Gaussian models, and not to be combined with a family object that names a link other than logit or log.

denominator

Optional denominator for binomial distributions, or exposure for Poisson and negative binomial ones, the mean of a count being the exposure times the inverse link of the linear predictor. Passed as a bare/unquoted column name present in data. If not provided, defaults to 1.

model_crs

Optional CRS (e.g. an EPSG code) used internally for model fitting. If data is already in a projected CRS and model_crs is not provided, the data are used as-is. If data are in longitude/latitude and model_crs is not provided, the data are automatically reprojected to the CRS from propose_crs(), a UTM zone or a projection centred on the data, and a message names the CRS and the units of distance. If provided, model_crs must be a projected (not longitude/latitude) CRS. A warning of class riskmap_warning_crs is raised when the CRS used distorts distances by more than 1% over the data.

distance_units

Character string, either "km" or "m", indicating the units used for internal coordinate distances and spatial parameters such as phi. The coordinates in the returned data retain the linear units declared by its CRS. Defaults to "km".

control_mcmc

Control parameters for MCMC sampling for binomial or Poisson models. Must be an object of class RiskMap_control_mcmc as returned by set_control_mcmc().

control_mcml

Control parameters for adaptive Monte Carlo maximum likelihood estimation. Must be returned by set_control_mcml().

seed

Optional non-negative integer that seeds every random step of a binomial or Poisson fit: the Monte Carlo samples of the estimation and the final conditional samples. When NULL (the default), one integer is drawn from the session's random number generator, so set.seed() before the call also reproduces the fit. The seed used is returned as seed. The caller's random number state is otherwise left unchanged. Ignored for Gaussian models, which have no random step.

return_samples

Logical indicating whether to draw and retain conditional samples at the fitted parameters. These samples are used to compute fitted values. If FALSE, final sampling is skipped and fitted values are not computed. Defaults to TRUE. Ignored for Gaussian models.

messages

Logical indicating whether to print messages, and a line for each stage of Monte Carlo maximum likelihood as described in riskmap_progress. Defaults to the option RiskMap.messages, or TRUE if it is not set.

fix_var_me

Optional fixed value for the measurement error variance when fitting a Gaussian model. When not provided, the value will be estimated, but cannot be if each location only has one sample and the nugget term in gp() is also set to TRUE.

start_pars

Optional list of starting values for model parameters:

beta

regression coefficients

sigma2

spatial process variance

tau2

nugget effect variance

phi

spatial correlation scale

sigma2_me

measurement error variance - only for Gaussian models

sigma2_re

random effects variances - only when random effects are included

theta

size of the negative binomial family - only when it is estimated (see negative_binomial())

Value

An object of class RiskMap containing the fitted model and relevant information:

estimate

Estimated parameters as a named list: beta (named regression coefficients on the scale of the supplied covariates), sigma2, phi, nu2 \(= \tau^2/\sigma^2\) when the nugget is estimated, sigma2_me for Gaussian models with an estimated measurement error variance, theta for negative binomial models whose size is estimated, stored as \(\log(1/\theta)\), the opposite sign to the logarithm of a variance (coef() gives \(\theta\)), and sigma2_re (a named vector, one entry per random effect) when random effects are included. Keeping these in separate list elements - rather than one flat named vector - avoids a covariate whose name collides with a parameter name (e.g. a covariate literally called "sigma2") corrupting name-based lookups. covariance is estimated as one joint matrix over every parameter; its rows/columns are named to match unlist(estimate).

grad_MLE

Gradient of the maximum likelihood function

covariance

Covariance

log_lik

Log likelihood

y

Response variable

D

Covariate matrix

coords

Unique spatial coordinates

ID_coords

Index of coordinates

re

Random effects if re() is included in formula

ID_re

Index of random effects if re() is included in formula

fix_tau2

Fixed nugget effect variance

fix_var_me

Fixed measurement error variance

family_parameters

For a negative binomial model whose size is held, the size as list(theta = ). Absent otherwise.

formula

Model formula

family

Response family

link_function

For binomial and Poisson models, the inverse link (inv), its first and second derivatives (d1 and d2) and the name of the link (link), such as "probit", which is NULL for an inverse given in invlink. NULL for Gaussian models.

distance_units

Units ("km" or "m") used for internal coordinate distances and spatial parameters

data

The sf data used for model fitting, in the CRS used internally

input_crs

The CRS of the input data

kappa

Spatial correlation parameter

units_m

The denominators or exposures of a binomial, Poisson or negative binomial model

cov_offset

Covariate offset

call

Matched call

S_samples

For non-Gaussian models, fresh conditional MCMC samples evaluated at the fitted parameters when return_samples is TRUE. These are not the reference samples used for MCML estimation. The first block is the location-level Gaussian effect (including the nugget when present), followed by any unstructured random-effect blocks.

linear_predictors

Conditional fitted linear predictors. For non-Gaussian models these are Monte Carlo means over the final-parameter latent samples and are NULL when return_samples = FALSE; for Gaussian models they use the conditional latent mean.

fitted_values

Conditional fitted response means. Binomial models return probabilities; Poisson and negative binomial models return expected counts and therefore include any supplied exposure in denominator. These are NULL for non-Gaussian models when return_samples = FALSE.

mcml_history

For non-Gaussian models, one entry per stage of certified Monte Carlo maximum likelihood (see set_control_mcml()), containing the sizes of the fitting and validation samples, the importance distribution used, the optimum of the fitting sample (fitted_estimate) and the corrected estimate (estimate), the optimizer result, the size of the correction, the certificate and its two parts (certificate_distance and certificate_radius), effective sample sizes and Pareto tail diagnostics of each sample, the outcome of the stage and its timing. A stage where the global importance distribution failed also holds why, in proposal_failure or, at the start of the first stage, start_failure: the reason, the number of refits and the last change of its factors. Estimates use the same parameterisation as estimate, with regression coefficients and spatial scale restored to the supplied covariate and distance units. NULL for Gaussian models.

mcml_certified

Whether the certificate of the returned estimate is within the tolerance. The certificate is an approximate 95% bound, in statistical standard errors, on the Monte Carlo error of the estimate, that is its distance from the maximum of the exact likelihood that the fit has located. It says nothing about whether that maximum is the highest. NULL for Gaussian models.

mcml_selected_iteration

The stage whose estimate is returned. NULL for Gaussian models.

seed

The seed used for the random steps of a binomial or Poisson fit, whether supplied or drawn. NULL for Gaussian models.

Details

Generalized linear Gaussian process models extend generalized linear models (GLMs) by incorporating spatial Gaussian processes to account for spatial correlation in the data. This function fits GLGPMs using maximum likelihood methods, allowing for Gaussian, binomial, Poisson and negative binomial response families. In the case of the binomial, Poisson and negative binomial families, a Monte Carlo maximum likelihood algorithm is used. A negative binomial model is fitted as the binomial model of its counts at each value of its size (see negative_binomial()).

The spatial Gaussian process is modeled with a Matern correlation function, which is flexible and commonly used in geostatistical modeling. The function supports both spatial covariates and unstructured random effects, providing a comprehensive framework to analyze spatially correlated data across different response distributions.

Additionally, the function allows for the inclusion of unstructured random effects, specified through the re() term in the model formula. These random effects can capture unexplained variability at specific locations beyond the fixed and spatial covariate effects, enhancing the model's flexibility in capturing complex spatial patterns.

The model_crs argument can be used to reproject the spatial coordinates to a different, projected CRS for model fitting. If data are in longitude/latitude and model_crs is not supplied, the coordinates are automatically reprojected to the CRS from propose_crs() and a message details the conversion; automatic projection is avoided for model_crs explicitly supplied in longitude/latitude, which raises an error. The distance_units argument controls whether distances between locations (and so parameters such as phi) are expressed in kilometers ("km", the default) or meters ("m").

The control_mcmc argument specifies the control parameters for MCMC sampling. This argument must be an object returned by set_control_mcmc(). Non-Gaussian models are fitted by certified Monte Carlo maximum likelihood (MCML), controlled by control_mcml (see set_control_mcml()). The estimate is corrected with an independent validation sample and certified with a second, fresh one, which bounds its Monte Carlo error in statistical standard errors, with an allowance for that sample's own error taken from it and from a replicate of it (see set_control_mcml()). The samples are enlarged only when the certificate exceeds the tolerance. Every stage is recorded in mcml_history, and a warning is issued if the tolerance is not met within the configured limits. Warnings are kept for what changes how a result is read, and check_fit() goes through all the checks on the computation, with what to do about any that need a look. The estimation samples and the final conditional samples are drawn from separate streams derived from seed, so glgpm(..., seed = fit$seed) reproduces a fit exactly.

The start_pars argument allows starting values to be supplied explicitly. Otherwise a binomial, Poisson or negative binomial model starts from RiskMap's defaults, which are the coefficients of the regression without latent effects, sigma2 = 1, phi at the 10th percentile of the distances between locations, and 1 for an estimated nugget variance and for the variance of each re() term. A model with the canonical link and without re() terms compares them with the estimates of a Gaussian model fitted to the empirical link of the data (the empirical logit of a binomial model), with one observation per location, the totals of the location where it has several records, and starts from the one with the higher Laplace approximation of the likelihood. summary.RiskMap() says which starting values a fit used and why.

See also

set_control_mcmc(), set_control_mcml(), summary.RiskMap, to_table

Examples


data(italy_sim)

# intercept only
fit <- glgpm(
  formula = y ~ gp(),
  data = italy_sim[1:100,],
  family = "gaussian",
  messages = FALSE
)

summary(fit)
#> ── Linear geostatistical model ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> glgpm(formula = y ~ gp(), data = italy_sim[1:100, ], family = "gaussian",
#>     messages = FALSE)
#> The identity link.
#> The limits are those of 95% confidence intervals.
#> 
#> Regression coefficients
#>             Estimate Lower limit Upper limit   StdErr z.value   p.value    
#> (Intercept)  9.32340     7.70078    10.94603  0.82788  11.262 < 2.2e-16 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Measurement error
#>                        Estimate Lower limit Upper limit
#> Measurement error var.  0.17859     0.13335      0.2392
#> 
#> Spatial Gaussian process, Matern correlation with kappa = 0.5
#>                          Estimate Lower limit Upper limit
#> Spatial process var.       4.8494      1.8196      12.924
#> Spatial corr. scale (km)  39.0150      2.7773     548.084
#> Variance of the nugget effect fixed at 0
#> 
#> Log-likelihood   8.618636
#> AIC             -9.237272

# add a covariate
fit <- glgpm(
  formula = y ~ gp() + pop_dens,
  data = italy_sim[1:100,],
  family = "gaussian",
  messages = FALSE
)

summary(fit)
#> ── Linear geostatistical model ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> glgpm(formula = y ~ gp() + pop_dens, data = italy_sim[1:100,
#>     ], family = "gaussian", messages = FALSE)
#> The identity link.
#> The limits are those of 95% confidence intervals.
#> 
#> Regression coefficients
#>               Estimate Lower limit Upper limit     StdErr z.value   p.value    
#> (Intercept) 7.70187620  6.37937916  9.02437323 0.67475578 11.4143 < 2.2e-16 ***
#> pop_dens    0.00046825  0.00023917  0.00069733 0.00011688  4.0063 6.168e-05 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Measurement error
#>                        Estimate Lower limit Upper limit
#> Measurement error var.  0.17853     0.13331      0.2391
#> 
#> Spatial Gaussian process, Matern correlation with kappa = 0.5
#>                          Estimate Lower limit Upper limit
#> Spatial process var.      1.77451     0.59997      5.2484
#> Spatial corr. scale (km) 75.04610     9.01027    625.0556
#> Variance of the nugget effect fixed at 0
#> 
#> Log-likelihood   14.34117
#> AIC             -18.68233

# add a random effect
fit <- glgpm(
  formula = y ~ gp() + re(province),
  data = italy_sim[1:100,],
  family = "gaussian",
  messages = FALSE
)

summary(fit)
#> ── Linear geostatistical model ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> glgpm(formula = y ~ gp() + re(province), data = italy_sim[1:100,
#>     ], family = "gaussian", messages = FALSE)
#> The identity link.
#> The limits are those of 95% confidence intervals.
#> 
#> Regression coefficients
#>             Estimate Lower limit Upper limit   StdErr z.value   p.value    
#> (Intercept)  9.34077     7.92351    10.75804  0.72311  12.918 < 2.2e-16 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Measurement error
#>                        Estimate Lower limit Upper limit
#> Measurement error var.  0.17859     0.13335      0.2392
#> 
#> Spatial Gaussian process, Matern correlation with kappa = 0.5
#>                          Estimate Lower limit Upper limit
#> Spatial process var.     0.438837    0.022556      8.5376
#> Spatial corr. scale (km) 0.917141    0.000000         Inf
#> Variance of the nugget effect fixed at 0
#> 
#> Unstructured random effects
#>                             Estimate Lower limit Upper limit
#> province (random eff. var.)   4.2742      1.4733        12.4
#> 
#> Log-likelihood   9.082286
#> AIC             -8.164572

# estimate the nugget
fit <- glgpm(
  formula = y ~ gp(nugget = TRUE),
  data = italy_sim[1:100,],
  family = "gaussian",
  messages = FALSE
)

summary(fit)
#> ── Linear geostatistical model ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> glgpm(formula = y ~ gp(nugget = TRUE), data = italy_sim[1:100,
#>     ], family = "gaussian", messages = FALSE)

#> The limits are those of 95% confidence intervals.
#> 
#> Regression coefficients
#>             Estimate Lower limit Upper limit   StdErr z.value   p.value    
#> (Intercept)  9.32340     7.70078    10.94603  0.82788  11.262 < 2.2e-16 ***

#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Measurement error
#>                        Estimate Lower limit Upper limit
#> Measurement error var.  0.17859     0.13335      0.2392
#> 
#> Spatial Gaussian process, Matern correlation with kappa = 0.5
#>                            Estimate Lower limit Upper limit
#> Spatial process var.     4.8494e+00  1.8196e+00      12.924
#> Spatial corr. scale (km) 3.9015e+01  2.7773e+00     548.084
#> Variance of the nugget   7.3615e-08  0.0000e+00         Inf
#> 
#> Log-likelihood   8.618636
#> AIC             -7.237272

# binomial model
data(loaloa)

# reduce iterations to speed up the fit, and set a
# seed for reproducibility
control_mcmc <- set_control_mcmc(n_sim = 100,
                                 burnin = 20)

fit <- glgpm(NO_INF ~ gp(),
             data = loaloa[1:50,],
             denominator = NO_EXAM,
             family = "binomial",
             control_mcmc = control_mcmc,
             seed = 42,
             messages = FALSE)
#> ℹ `data` are in longitude and latitude, so they are projected to a custom
#>   oblique Mercator projection ("RiskMap oblique Mercator 11.5E 5N azimuth -72.5
#>   k0 0.9998") for fitting, with distances in km. No UTM zone keeps distances
#>   within 0.5% over them. Set `model_crs` to choose the projection.

summary(fit)
#> ── Binomial geostatistical model ───────────────────────────────────────────────
#> glgpm(formula = NO_INF ~ gp(), data = loaloa[1:50, ], family = "binomial",
#>     denominator = NO_EXAM, control_mcmc = control_mcmc, seed = 42,
#>     messages = FALSE)
#> The canonical logit link.
#> The limits are those of 95% confidence intervals.
#> 
#> Regression coefficients
#>             Estimate Lower limit Upper limit  StdErr z.value   p.value    
#> (Intercept)  -2.1233     -3.2385     -1.0081  0.5690 -3.7317 0.0001902 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Spatial Gaussian process, Matern correlation with kappa = 0.5
#>                          Estimate Lower limit Upper limit
#> Spatial process var.       2.1220      0.9347      4.8173
#> Spatial corr. scale (km) 102.1364     34.7203    300.4537
#> Variance of the nugget effect fixed at 0
#> 
#> Log-likelihood  -2018.33
#> 
#> Monte Carlo maximum likelihood
#> ✔ Certified. The Monte Carlo error of the estimate is within 0.0055 statistical
#>   standard errors (an approximate 95% bound, tolerance 0.1).
#> ℹ The starting values came from a Gaussian fit to the transformed data, which
#>   the Laplace approximation of the likelihood preferred to RiskMap's defaults.
#> ✔ No check needs a look. See `check_fit()` for the details.
